# Offline oracle fixtures

The audit ran the unmodified original matching module and CLI under Python 3.11.2 (Unicode 14.0.0), pandas 3.0.6, RapidFuzz 3.14.6, regex 2026.9.29 and Ray 2.59.0. Dependencies were resolved with `uv run --no-project --with pandas --with ray --with regex --with rapidfuzz --with pytest`. All original dependency constraints were satisfied.

For CLI comparisons only, Ray's `init`, `shutdown`, `put`, `get` and remote-task wrapper were replaced in memory with synchronous local equivalents. The original CLI, pandas CSV parsing and matching functions were otherwise unchanged. No network site or running Ray cluster was used. Rust threading is tested separately by comparing ordered output across chunk and batch sizes. Fixture expectations do not depend on logs, timestamps or Ray scheduling.

- `input.csv`, `reference.csv`, `expected.csv`: existing baseline CLI fixture, preserved.
- `scores.csv`: 2,584 pairs with RapidFuzz `fuzz.WRatio` scores. Four explicit cases and 2,500 seeded random short strings (seed 479, characters `abc řá`, TAB and U+001C), plus 80 pairs longer than 64 code points (seed 33). Covers whitespace tokenization, Unicode letters, token sets, partial alignments, length scaling and floating-point score parity. Scores are compared within 1e-9.
- `unicode-oracle.csv`: 210 original/reference pairs, including ten explicit cases and 200 random cases (seed 719). Columns record original Python diacritic removal, grapheme count, lowercase index key, mark merging, diacritic application, mark count and Czech classification. Includes decomposed marks, uppercase, dotted I, Greek, Indic clusters, joiners and emoji.
- `corrections-oracle.csv`: 612 complete correction results, with and without a populated index. Six explicit names and 300 seeded mutations (seed 719, following generation of the Unicode corpus). References are separated by LF inside a quoted CSV field; their order is preserved. This covers candidate selection as well as scores.
- `cli-oracle.csv`: 24 offline CLI scenarios. Binary input, reference and output are hex encoded so NUL, CR and invalid UTF-8 remain unambiguous. `-` means no output file. Both original Python and accepted Rust exit codes/output are retained. The Rust test uses the accepted Rust columns; Python columns preserve the evidence for intentional differences. Differences are NUL preservation, safer CR quoting and rejection of over-wide rows. All other outputs and exit codes match. CLI tests also cover failures, aliases, numeric syntax and large data beyond this corpus.

Oracle files are data, so they remain usable after removal of the Python implementation. Test case `long_identical_fuzzy_strings_and_recent_unicode` separately records the intentional Unicode database difference for U+1C89, outside the parity corpus. See the repository report for before/after findings and limitations.
